skill.name: pytest-mastery
skill.description: Guidance for running, writing, and debugging pytest tests with uv, including fixtures, parametrization, coverage, and FastAPI testing patterns.
skill.summary: Run, write, and debug pytest suites with uv and FastAPI examples.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline commands, and test-only FastAPI examples. One confirmed issue remains: scripts/run_tests.py executes uv run pytest through subprocess.call with forwarded user arguments, which is expected for a test runner but still executes local code.

remediation.issue: The test runner executes an external pytest command with forwarded arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run scripts/run_tests.py only inside trusted projects, and consider allowlisting supported modes and options for automated use.

remediation.issue: The FastAPI database example writes to a local SQLite file when copied directly.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a temporary directory or in-memory SQLite example for tests that should leave no persistent database file.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is http://test inside an httpx AsyncClient configured with ASGITransport for in-process FastAPI tests. It is a placeholder base URL, not an outbound network destination.
The value is a documented test-only SQLite URL named TEST_DATABASE_URL. It is not read from the environment and does not expose credentials or a production database.
The create_engine call consumes the same local TEST_DATABASE_URL example for isolated tests. No environment variable or secret-bearing production connection string is present.
The SQLite path is part of a FastAPI testing example and points to a local throwaway test database. The skill does not include an actual database file or sensitive data.

The helper script invokes uv run pytest through subprocess.call and forwards user-supplied pytest arguments. shell=False limits shell injection, but it still executes local project test code and plugins, so this is a real external command risk.

high_findings.title: Python subprocess.call
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper script invokes uv run pytest through subprocess.call and forwards user-supplied pytest arguments. shell=False limits shell injection, but it still executes local project test code and plugins, so this is a real external command risk.

content.value_statement: Python teams need repeatable tests, fixtures, coverage, and FastAPI patterns. This skill gives practical pytest guidance with uv commands and focused examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows uv commands for running all tests, single files, single tests, filtered tests, and coverage reports.
Explains pytest discovery rules, fixture scopes, shared conftest fixtures, and parametrized tests.
Provides common pytest options for verbosity, tracebacks, markers, last-failed runs, and parallel execution.
Includes FastAPI testing patterns for TestClient, async httpx clients, database fixtures, dependency overrides, and authentication.
Includes a helper script with quick, full, coverage, failed, and watch test modes.
Covers debugging workflows with long tracebacks, pdb, local variables, and last-failed test selection.
limitations: Assumes a Python project that uses uv and pytest.
Examples must be adapted to the user project structure and application imports.
The helper script does not sandbox test execution or third-party pytest plugins.
FastAPI examples are reference patterns, not a complete application test suite.

use_cases.title: Add Pytest to a Python Project
use_cases.description: Set up pytest with uv, create initial test files, and run a useful default test command.

use_cases.title: Test FastAPI Endpoints
use_cases.description: Build tests for sync endpoints, async endpoints, dependencies, authentication, uploads, and error responses.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Test Commands
use_cases.description: Use shared pytest modes for quick checks, full runs, coverage reports, and failed-test reruns.

prompt_templates.title: Run My Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mastery to show the uv commands I should run for all tests, one test file, and one test function.

prompt_templates.title: Create Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mastery to design pytest fixtures for my Python module, including fixture scope and conftest placement.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mastery to add parametrized tests and recommend pytest coverage commands for my src package.

prompt_templates.title: Plan FastAPI Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pytest-mastery to create a FastAPI test plan with TestClient, async httpx tests, database isolation, dependency overrides, and authentication checks.

output_examples.input: I need to run only the failing tests with useful output.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a last-failed pytest run with verbose output and a shorter traceback, then suggests a full run after fixes pass.

output_examples.input: I need FastAPI tests that avoid using the real database.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a test database fixture, a dependency override for the application database session, and cleanup after each test.

output_examples.input: I want better coverage for similar validation cases.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests parametrized pytest cases, a coverage command for the src package, and a minimum coverage threshold for CI.

best_practices: Keep test fixtures small, named clearly, and scoped to the minimum lifetime needed.
Run focused tests during development, then run the full suite with coverage before merging.
Use dependency overrides and isolated databases for FastAPI tests that touch state.
anti_patterns: Do not point tests at production databases, services, or credentials.
Do not hide flaky tests with broad skip markers instead of fixing the cause.
Do not run helper scripts in untrusted repositories without reviewing the test code first.

faq.question: Does this skill require uv?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands use uv to run pytest and manage development dependencies.

faq.question: Can it help write new pytest tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers fixtures, parametrization, discovery rules, markers, and practical test structure.

faq.question: Does it support FastAPI testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TestClient, async httpx, database fixtures, dependency overrides, authentication, uploads, and websockets.

faq.question: Does the helper script sandbox test execution?
faq.answer: No. It runs pytest in the local project, so tests and plugins execute with normal local permissions.

faq.question: Can it produce coverage reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents terminal, HTML, XML, and threshold-based coverage commands through pytest-cov.

faq.question: Is this a complete test framework?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance and a small runner script for pytest workflows in existing Python projects.
